caption:
5 tax facts most people have backwards.

1. A $1,000 deduction doesn't put $1,000 back in your pocket. It lowers your taxable income, so on the 30% rate (2026–27, $45,001–$135,000) it saves about $300, or $320 with the 2% Medicare levy.

2. A higher bracket only taxes the dollars above the threshold. In 2026–27 the 37% rate starts at $135,001, so a pay rise that crosses it still leaves you better off.

3. Individuals generally have 2 years to amend a return, counted from the day after your notice of assessment. Sole traders get 4 years for 2024–25 and later.

4. Salary-sacrificed super is taxed at 15% in your fund, not at your marginal rate, while you stay within the $32,500 concessional cap (2026–27, includes your employer's super). The catch: it's locked away until preservation age, and if your income plus contributions tops $250,000, Division 293 tax applies.

5. The working-from-home fixed rate method needs a record of the actual hours you work from home, kept as you go (timesheets, rosters, a diary). An estimate won't be accepted.

Which number did you have backwards? Tell us in the comments.
